subject: Decision Making
title: Prediction Markets
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Prediction Markets.

hook.text: Prediction markets let people bet real money on future events. The price becomes a probability estimate.

buildup.text: If a contract pays $1 when Event X happens and trades at $0.70, the market estimates a 70 percent probability.

discovery.text: Prediction markets outperform polls, pundits, and committees. Skin in the game forces honest estimates over wishful.

twist.text: Google and HP ran internal prediction markets. Employees predicted product launches better than the executives leading.

climax.text: Money forces honesty. When you must bet, you stop cheerleading and start estimating. Incentives align with accuracy.

punchline.text: Bet real money, get honest forecasts. Prediction markets monetize truth.

quiz.question: Why do prediction markets outperform expert committees?
options: Real money forces honest estimates instead of wishful thinking or social pressure
